headline: Discussed winter heating assistance, utility shutoff help, and weatherization programs for seniors and low-income households; no votes taken.
summary: Discussion covered the Home Energy Assistance Program, help for households facing utility shutoffs, and a developing one-time $600 heating assistance program for certain middle-income oil users. No formal recommendations or votes were made.

Public Portion 
 1. Fuel assistance resources for seniors and fixed-income/low-income families 
On October 15, 2026, the Joint Health and Human Services and Public Safety Committee, 
chaired by Councilors Brian Santaniello and Gerry Martin, met to discuss winter fuel assistance 
programs and available resources for Springfield residents. Maria Rosario of Valley Opportunity 
Council (VOC) outlined the Home Energy Assistance Program, which helps eligible low-income 
households pay for heating costs, including oil, gas, and electricity. Eligibility and benefit 
amounts are based on household size and income. Applications are available by telephone, in 
person, or online, with processing taking approximately 45 business days beginning November 
1. Returning participants receive annual renewal applications but must complete and return them 
to maintain assistance. 
 
Discussion addressed assistance for households facing utility shutoffs, including payments 
toward required deposits and coordination with Eversource on payment arrangements. VOC also 
described a developing one-time $600 heating assistance program for certain middle-income 
households using oil, along with referrals to Way Finders, the Salvation Army, and Catholic 
Charities when additional assistance is needed. Springfield Partners for Community Action 
provides weatherization services to eligible households referred by VOC, including home energy 
assessments, insulation, air sealing, and other energy-efficiency improvements. 
 
The committee discussed improving public awareness through the City's website, community 
outreach, and senior centers. VOC reported providing intake training to 21 senior centers to 
assist older residents with applications and documentation. Additional discussion addressed 
anticipated winter demand, program funding, and coordination among community organizations 
to connect residents with available resources. No formal recommendations or votes were made. 
The meeting adjourned at 1:30 p.m.
